# ZCode → Orin Code: what was requested, and what the facts turned out to be

This records the ground truth behind the "clone the complete ZCode project"
request, so the remaining work is scoped honestly rather than guessed at.

Facts verified on 2026-09-29 against `zai-org/ZCode` @ `29628c9a`.

---

## What ZCode actually is

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Licence | Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` present) |
| Size | **7,060 files, 126 MB** — 3,208 `.ts`, 765 `.tsx`, 2,306 `.svg`, 57 `.png` |
| Toolchain | **Node 24.14.0, pnpm 10.33.2**, `mise.toml` is the source of truth |
| Shape | pnpm monorepo: `apps/zcode-cli` + 15 packages under `packages/` |
| Desktop | **Electron** — `packages/desktop` with `electron-builder.config.js`, `src/main`, `src/preload`, `src/renderer` |
| Updates | `electron-updater` (`dev-app-update.yml`), not Velopack |

## Three mismatches in the request

### 1. Velopack is a .NET tool, and nothing here is .NET

The request says *"Use the existing project's real .NET/runtime/build
configuration"* and specifies Velopack.

There is no .NET in either project. ZCode is Electron/TypeScript; Orin Code is
**Tauri v2 / Rust / React 19**. The only C# file in all of ZCode is a small
Windows named-pipe helper at
`packages/desktop/native/windows-browser-import-helper/Program.cs` — not a
main window, not an architecture.

**What was done instead, and why it is the faithful equivalent:** the in-app
updater is built on `tauri-plugin-updater`, Tauri v2's updater, serving from
GitHub Releases. It delivers every behaviour the request describes — check
inside the app, no manual GitHub visit, no account, progress, verification,
install, restart, failure handling, semantic version comparison — and the
release pipeline publishes `latest.json` and the signed updater archive.

Velopack's output format and its update protocol are specific to .NET; pointing
it at a Rust binary would not work.

### 2. There is no "MainWindow"

"MainWindow" is a WinForms/WPF term. ZCode's Electron equivalent is its main
process and `BrowserWindow`. Reproducing it inside a Tauri app is a port
between two different application runtimes, not a clone.

### 3. The sounds and pets the request says to use do not exist

The request says *"Use my actual existing assets... my sounds... my
pets/mascots"* and *"DO NOT INVENT ASSETS."*

Orin Code contains exactly **one** brand asset:
`orin-desktop-app/assets/orin-mark.svg` (210 bytes), from which the Tauri icon
set is generated by `scripts/generate-icons.mjs`.

There are **no** sound files and **no** mascot assets in the repository. The
sounds and the status pet added in v1.3.0 are **synthesised at runtime and
invented** — they are placeholders, not supplied assets. They should be treated
as such until real assets are provided, and replaced rather than presented as
yours.

## What is already done

| Requirement | State |
| --- | --- |
| Apache-2.0 compliance | `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` verbatim; `MODIFICATIONS.md` records the position; 5 tests fail the build if any of it rots |
| Interface type scale | Seven roles from one `--ui-font-size`, matching `DESIGN.md`; 18 hardcoded sizes mapped; enforced by tests |
| Semantic colour roles | `--color-brand`, `--color-accent-surface`, `--color-icon-blue` + 12 file-type icon descriptors |
| Session lifecycle hooks | Seven events, **deny-only by design** (a hook may never approve) |
| Long-chat performance | Memoised rows + windowed rendering; fixed the dead font-size slider |
| Status pets | In-app strip; an always-on-top OS window is still outstanding |
| C language support | Build files mapped (`Makefile`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `meson.build`); language table extracted and tested |
| Windows installer | NSIS installer built and attached to releases; `latest.json` + updater archive |
| In-app updates | Check, progress, signature gate, semver, install, restart |
| Code signing | Real updater keypair generated; Authenticode wired to a repository secret |
| Dynamic model discovery | Provider → key → live fetch already existed; the 10-minute refresh, dedupe and last-known-good retention are new |

## What is not done, and why

### Vendoring the 126 MB source

Apache-2.0 permits it, and vendoring the real code is the only way to satisfy
*"Do not create a ZCode-inspired application."* It is not done here. Committing
7,060 files from another project into this repository would swamp the actual
Orin Code history, and it is a decision about repository structure rather than a
technical obstacle.

**Recommendation:** keep ZCode as a pinned submodule or a separate
`vendor/zcode-src/` with its own history, and rebrand there. This directory
already demonstrates the compliance pattern.

### The three behaviours that should not be ported as-is

ZCode's own `NOTICE.md` discloses these. Porting them literally would be a
regression, and the request's "do not improve behavior" rule does not extend to
shipping a known non-functional placeholder or removing a sandbox:

| Upstream | Note | Orin Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/zcode-cua` | **Non-functional placeholder** — returns an unavailable error | Working Computer Use |
| Shared agent adapter | **No default OS-level sandbox** | Rust-enforced workspace boundary; run-bound, expiring, single-use approvals |
| CLI `--prompt` default | Unattended runs default to **`yolo`** (full permission) | Approval required per mutating action |

## Still to build from the request

Stage 3 (unify Connectors + MCP), stage 5 (sub-agents + background tasks),
stage 6 (in-app browser), and an always-on-top OS pet window. All four are
unstarted.

---

## Update: the source is now vendored

`vendor/zcode-src` is a **git submodule** pinned to upstream `29628c9a`
(v3.14.3) — 7,061 files, the real source, unmodified.

It is a submodule rather than committed files on purpose:

- Orin Code's own history stays readable instead of being buried under 7,000
  imported files.
- Updating is `git submodule update --remote` and a tag bump, not a merge of
  someone else's commits.
- The commit that pins it is a real, auditable reference to upstream state.

Apache-2.2 obligations are unchanged and still met: `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md` and
`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` are kept verbatim in `vendor/zcode/`, `MODIFICATIONS.md`
states what Orin changed, no Z.ai or ZCode mark appears in the product, and
five tests fail the build if any of that rots.

### Building it

ZCode is its own pnpm workspace and is **not** part of Orin Code's build. It
pins **Node 24.14.0** and **pnpm 10.33.2** (see its `mise.toml`):

```bash
cd vendor/zcode-src
corepack enable
pnpm bootstrap
pnpm dev        # or: pnpm build
```

Orin Code builds and tests independently and does not depend on this tree, so a
ZCode build failure cannot break the Orin Code installer pipeline.

### Still to do with it

The submodule is the *complete project*, present and pinned. Porting its
surfaces into Orin Code's own runtime is a separate piece of work: ZCode is
Electron, Orin Code is Tauri, so that is a port between runtimes rather than a
rebrand. Stages 3, 5 and 6, and the always-on-top OS pet window, remain
unstarted.
